subtype: Approach: add disclosure and keep a record of use [Revision]
passage:
"Thomas, before you go. Which parts of this essay did you write yourself?"

"Most of it, Professor Sonali. I used the tool for the outline and to smooth two paragraphs."

"And where does it say that?"

"It doesn't." He shifted in his chair. "I didn't think it mattered."

"It matters because I can't tell which ideas are yours."

Thomas nodded slowly. "Okay. I'll keep a note from now on."

A week later he stood at her door again with a printout. "There's a line at the end this time: 'Outline suggested by an AI tool; paragraphs two and five edited with it.' And I've saved the prompts."

Sonali smiled. "Now I know exactly what is yours."

qa.q: What did Thomas add at the end of the essay?
qa.a: A line saying the outline was suggested by an AI tool and that paragraphs two and five were edited with it.

qa.q: How did Thomas feel when Sonali asked where his essay said the tool was used?
qa.a: Thomas felt awkward and a little caught out, shown by shifting in his chair and admitting he had not thought it mattered.

qa.q: What could Thomas do next if he is unsure whether a use of the tool needs mentioning, and why?
qa.a: Thomas could ask Professor Sonali or check the course rules, because an early question is safer than a surprise later.

qa.q: How might Sonali see the extra line in Thomas's essay?
qa.a: Sonali sees an honest record that lets her tell which ideas are Thomas's own, and it rebuilds her trust.

grounding: After a professor's question, the student notes where AI helped and adds an acknowledgment, which clarifies what is their own work.
